original_question: A sail is the boundary of C \ LS, where C is a cone of a hyperplane arrangement and LS is the union of all subsets U similar to a chosen model subset S that avoid a chosen subset L. Classify all combinatorially possible types of faces that can occur on such sails, especially for Klein polyhedra where S is a basis n-simplex and L = Z^n intersected with the punctured cone C.
target_in_paper: Section 3.2, Problem 3: "Classify all combinatorial possible types of faces," read with the sail construction in Section 2.1, Definitions 2.1-2.2, and the Klein-polyhedron specialization in Section 2.2, Definition 2.4. The nearby Problem 5 is a related sharpening, but not the primary target. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1712.01450))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the right object and the right question: it uses the general sail construction from Definition 2.2 (cone C, model subset S, forbidden set L, and subsets U similar to S that avoid L), and it correctly singles out the Klein case where S is a basis n-simplex and L is the punctured lattice cone (C\{0}) ∩ Z^n. It also matches the official emphasis of Problem 3, which asks for classification of face types and is said to target mostly Klein polyhedra. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1712.01450))
missing_details: The ambient setting should be stated explicitly: an arrangement of n hyperplanes through the origin in R^n, in general position, and C must be one of the cones of that arrangement. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1712.01450))
The word "similar" is not ordinary Euclidean similarity; it means similarity via a stretching of the cone in the sense of Definition 2.1. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1712.01450))

To make the sail definition stand alone, one should explicitly say that Sail_{S,L}(C) is the boundary of the set obtained from C by deleting the union of all subsets U contained in C that are similar to S and satisfy U ∩ L = empty. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1712.01450))

For the Klein specialization, the paper uses the punctured cone notation C\{0}; your draft alludes to it but does not explicitly identify this as the paper's standard notation in the setup. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1712.01450))

Problem 3 asks only for combinatorial possible types of faces; it does not, at this point, ask for a full classification up to integer congruence or for all lattice invariants of faces. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1712.01450))

The paper says this question targets mostly Klein polyhedra, so a stand-alone reformulation should keep that emphasis rather than sounding like an equally developed problem for every possible choice of S and L. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1712.01450))

Nearby context refines the broad face-classification problem by separating faces at integer distance 1 from the origin from faces at larger integer distance (view-obstacle problems); this sharpening is absent from the draft. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1712.01450))

The paper also notes that for some choices of S and L sails can be stratified surfaces with singularities, so the notion of "faces" is cleanest when the question is stated in the polyhedral/Klein setting. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1712.01450))

No algebraic conditions such as homogeneity, polynomial degree, field characteristic, or nilpotency are involved here; the problem is purely geometric in R^n with lattice Z^n. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1712.01450))
refined_question: Fix n >= 2. Let A be an arrangement of n hyperplanes through the origin in R^n in general position, let C be one of its cones, and let Sail_{S,L}(C) be the sail of Definition 2.2, obtained by deleting from C the union of all subsets U contained in C that are similar to S via stretchings of C and satisfy U ∩ L = empty, and then taking the boundary. In the Klein-polyhedron case, where S is a basis n-simplex of C and L = (C\{0}) ∩ Z^n, classify the combinatorial types of faces that can occur on Sail_{S,L}(C). ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1712.01450))
justification: The draft is aiming at Problem 3 almost verbatim: Section 3.2 calls it the central question of the subsection and states "Classify all combinatorial possible types of faces," immediately adding that the question targets mostly Klein polyhedra. The notation in the draft comes directly from Definitions 2.1-2.2 and the Klein specialization from Definition 2.4. Problem 4 is narrower (empty simplices), while Problem 5 is a more specific nearby realizability refinement about which n-gons can occur as faces and about integer-distance subcases, so the closest official formulation is Problem 3, not those neighboring problems. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1712.01450))
